title: Kids turned the comment section of an NPR podcast into a group chat
tldr: Middle schoolers colonized the Spotify comment section of NPR's Wild Card as an impromptu group chat, and This American Life dug into why. A vivid, current signal of how young audiences repurpose platforms in unexpected ways.
angle: Write about how audiences hack platform features for community — and what content owners should do when their comment section becomes a group chat.

title: From brand deals to equity deals: creators want a stake, not just a fee
tldr: Creators are increasingly negotiating equity and ownership rather than one-off fees, signaling a structural shift in creator-brand economics. Reframes the whole influencer partnership model.
angle: Explore what it means for brands when creators become equity stakeholders, not vendors — the end of the transactional influencer era.

title: An astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions: Court records show what Microsoft and OpenAI actually thought about AI training
tldr: Newly unredacted court filings reveal internal language calling AI training data 'the largest theft of labor in human history.' A major reputational and legal flashpoint for how content is used to train models.
angle: Unpack what the leaked internal framing means for publishers' leverage and content ownership in the AI era.

title: More Companies Are Launching AI Writing Policies as the Slop War Heats Up
tldr: Brands are rolling out formal AI writing policies as 'slop' backlash grows, forcing governance decisions about human vs. machine content. Directly relevant to content governance and human-centered content.
angle: Draft a practical AI content governance policy framework — where to draw the human line and why.

title: DoorDash bluntly admits 'we screwed up' in $131.5 million settlement (plus MrBeast on video)
tldr: The Scoop covers DoorDash's blunt public mea culpa in a major settlement plus MrBeast's take on video's power. A useful crisis-comms tone case study alongside creator insight.
angle: Analyze the 'we screwed up' plain-language apology as a crisis-comms playbook — when bluntness beats corporate hedging.

title: How Brooklinen Built an Influencer Marketing Strategy Around Life at Home
tldr: A concrete campaign breakdown of Brooklinen's first in-house celebrity-led effort anchored in relatable 'life at home' content. Practical case study for authentic, human-centered brand storytelling.
angle: Break down why 'life at home' framing outperforms polished celebrity gloss for DTC brands.

title: I Tracked 13,184 AI Citations Across 4 LLMs: Here's What I Learned
tldr: An original data study of over 13,000 AI citations across four LLMs revealing which sources models actually cite. Rare hard data for anyone thinking about GEO and content visibility.
angle: Turn the citation data into a content strategy: what actually makes your content get cited by LLMs.

title: The state of social media in 2026: Data from Sprout's latest pulse survey
tldr: Fresh survey data on shifting social media behaviors and marketer priorities heading into 2026. Useful benchmark for audience-consumption trends.
angle: Pull the 2-3 most counterintuitive stats and build a POV on where social attention is actually going in 2026.

title: Substack Notes is Now In Buffer (and how one podcaster works social one day a month)
tldr: Buffer added Substack Notes scheduling plus a case study of a creator batching a month of posts in a single day. Concrete workflow and cross-posting playbook for lean content ops.
angle: Write about the 'one day a month' batching model as a sustainable alternative to always-on content grind.

title: Media as a distinctive brand asset
tldr: Argues that media placements themselves can build brand associations the way logos and jingles do — a rethink of owned/paid media as brand-building infrastructure. A genuinely fresh strategic frame.
angle: Explore treating recurring media formats as distinctive brand assets in your own content architecture.

title: Why 'AI Productivity Gains' Is the Wrong Pitch for Every Stakeholder Above You
tldr: Argues that pitching AI as productivity gains fails with CMOs, CFOs and legal — and offers audience-specific reframes to defend budget and headcount. Sharp internal-comms/positioning advice.
angle: Build a stakeholder-by-stakeholder messaging matrix for selling AI content investment internally.

title: AI Citations and the Second Golden Age of Content Marketing
tldr: Argues that old-school content marketing craft is exactly what earns AI citations, framing this as a renaissance rather than a threat. Optimistic, practical take on GEO.
angle: Make the case that fundamentals — not tricks — are the new SEO in the AI-answer era.

title: Бренды и агентства: почему старый формат сотрудничества зашел в тупик
tldr: A KITCHEN and RLVNT study on why beautiful creative without data no longer works and what clients and agencies must agree on before starting. Fresh Russian-market perspective on the creative-data tension.
angle: Contrast the data-vs-creative debate with your own view on where craft still wins.

title: When disaster strikes, newsrooms scramble. A new website aims to help tame the chaos.
tldr: A new tool helps newsrooms coordinate disaster coverage, born from lessons of Hurricane Helene. Interesting operational case study in editorial workflow under crisis conditions.
angle: Draw lessons for any content team on building crisis-mode editorial workflows before you need them.

title: Is This The End For Influencer Marketing?
tldr: Questions whether the influencer marketing model is peaking or breaking, amid saturation and shifting consumer trust. A timely provocation on a maturing channel.
angle: Argue what replaces influencer marketing — creator equity, EGC, or something more human.
